metadata.name: grant-access
metadata.description: Somebody asked for temporary access to a production resource. A ROUTER decides the ceremony from the resource's tier, the level asked for, the hours asked for and the requester's own history: granted automatically, signed by a person first, or denied with the policy rule that said no. The access ledger is read at the start of the run and written at the end, so the `kind: "error"` edge out of `read-ledger` is not a hypothetical — it is the FIRST run of this command, where there is no ledger to read yet.

labels.reads-as: the router picks the CEREMONY; the arms are how much human a decision needs
labels.residue-error-arm: `prior` and `first-grant` are mutually exclusive BY CONSTRUCTION — one is the `seq` target of `read-ledger` and the other its `error` target, and no run can take both. The compiler cannot see that: `GRAPH010_CONCURRENT_WRITE` calls them concurrent writers of `history` and refuses `replace`. `merge_object` is the workaround, and it is a workaround — the channel holds one contribution on every run that has ever been measured. See F1 of docs/workflow-port-2026-09-22b.md.
labels.residue-static-approvers: `sign` names `u:you` because `approval.approvers` is a STATIC list in the graph, while the people who may actually sign are `decision.owners` — read out of access/policy.json at run time. The gate therefore shows the right owners and accepts the wrong signature. See F3.
labels.compiles-silent: This graph prints NO diagnostic at all — measured, not assumed. `deny` is terminal and writes no declared output, but GRAPH002_DEAD_END does not fire on it: `decision` is a declared output and `weigh` writes it on the same path. An earlier draft of these labels claimed the warning, which was a label asserting something no run had established.
labels.residue-blind-error-arm: THE PRODUCT GAP, AND THE DEFENCE THIS GRAPH PAYS FOR IT. An error arm is handed no reason: the failed node writes nothing and no channel carries the code or the message, so `first-grant` cannot tell "there is no ledger yet" from "the ledger is there and I could not read it". `codes` does not separate them either — a missing file, an unreadable file AND a path the sandbox refuses are all E_TOOL_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (measured; see F5). Undefended, `chmod 222 out/access-ledger.json` made the run report `succeeded` and REPLACED the ledger, destroying a prior grant. THE DEFENCE IS THE `look` NODE: fs.glob lists a file fs.read cannot open, so `weigh` refuses when the listing is non-empty and the history came from the error arm. It is narrow and not a closure — it works only because this failing read has a PATH another read-only tool can ask about, and it has a TOCTOU window — so F5 stays a PRODUCT entry and this is its cost.
labels.compensation-fires-without-an-edge: MEASURED, and worth knowing before you add a `compensation` edge you do not need: when `write-ledger` fails after `write-grant` succeeded, the engine rolls the grant write back on its own — `fs.write` declares `compensation: {tool: "fs.restore"}`, and `loom trace` shows `loom.tool (compensate) [ok]` under `write-grant`. out/grant.json still held the PREVIOUS run's grant afterwards. No compensation edge is declared in this graph and none is needed for that.
